content: 1. On October 1, 2010, a study was published in Lancet (Volume 51, Issue 7, Pages 855-864) by Raffi F, Babiker AG, Richert L, and colleagues. This study evaluated the efficacy of ritonavir-boosted darunavir combined with either raltegravir or tenofovir-emtricitabine in antiretroviral-naive adults infected with HIV-1. The results of this randomized, non-inferiority trial were assessed over a 96-week period as part of the NEAT001/ANRS143 study. 2. On November 29, 2014, Lancet (Volume 384, Issue 9958, Pages 1942-1951) published a study by Raffi F, Jaeger H, Quiros-Roldan E, and others. This research compared once-daily dolutegravir with twice-daily raltegravir in antiretroviral-naive adults with HIV-1 infection. The findings, derived from the SPRING-2 study, were based on a 96-week randomized, double-blind, non-inferiority trial. 3. On March 2, 2013, Lancet (Volume 381, Issue 9868, Pages 735-743) published the 48-week results of the SPRING-2 study by Raffi F, Rachlis A, Stellbrink HJ, and colleagues. This trial compared once-daily dolutegravir with raltegravir in antiretroviral-naive adults with HIV-1 infection. The study was randomized, double-blind, and designed to assess non-inferiority. 4. On November 15, 2010, Journal of Infectious Diseases (Volume 202, Issue 10, Pages 1529-1537) published a study by Ratsela A, Polis MA, Dhlomo S, and others. This randomized factorial trial compared four treatment regimens in treatment-naive HIV-infected individuals with AIDS and/or a CD4 cell count below 200 cells/μL in South Africa. 5. In February 2009, Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy (Volume 63, Issue 2, Pages 380-388) published a study by Rey D, Hoen B, Chavanet P, and colleagues. This research highlighted a high rate of early virological failure with the once-daily tenofovir/lamivudine/nevirapine combination in antiretroviral-naive HIV-1-infected patients. 6. In September-October 2011, HIV Clinical Trials (Volume 12, Issue 5, Pages 255-267) published the 48-week results of the PROGRESS study by Reynes J, Lawal A, Pulido F, and others. This study examined the non-inferiority, safety, and tolerability of lopinavir/ritonavir combined with raltegravir versus lopinavir/ritonavir combined with tenofovir/emtricitabine in antiretroviral-naive subjects. 7. In February 2013, AIDS Research and Human Retroviruses (Volume 29, Issue 2, Pages 256-265) published the 96-week results of the PROGRESS study by Reynes J, Trinh R, Pulido F, and colleagues. This study compared lopinavir/ritonavir combined with either raltegravir or tenofovir/emtricitabine in antiretroviral-naive subjects. 8. On April 1, 2008, Journal of Infectious Diseases (Volume 197, Issue 7, Pages 1006-1010) published a study by Ribaudo HJ, Kuritzkes DR, Lalama CM, and others. This research evaluated efavirenz-based regimens in treatment-naive patients with varying pretreatment HIV-1 RNA levels and CD4 cell counts. 9. On May 15, 2008, New England Journal of Medicine (Volume 358, Issue 20, Pages 2095-2106) published a study by Riddler SA, Haubrich R, DiRienzo AG, and colleagues. This research compared class-sparing regimens for the initial treatment of HIV-1 infection. 10. On November 11, 2012, Journal of the International AIDS Society (Volume 15, Article 23) published a study by Rockstroh J, De Jesus E, Henry K, and others. This research demonstrated the durable efficacy and differentiated safety of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF (QUAD) compared to ritonavir-boosted atazanavir plus emtricitabine/tenofovir DF at week 96 in treatment-naive HIV-1-infected patients. 11. In February 2012, HIV Medicine (Volume 13, Issue 2, Pages 127-131) published a study by Rockstroh J, Teppler H, Zhao J, and colleagues. This research assessed the safety and efficacy of raltegravir in patients co-infected with HIV-1 and hepatitis B and/or C virus. 12. On May 1, 2013, Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes (Volume 63, Issue 1, Pages 77-85) published the final 5-year results of the STARTMRK study by Rockstroh JK, Lennox JL, De Jesus E, and others. This study compared the long-term efficacy and safety of raltegravir versus efavirenz when combined with tenofovir/emtricitabine in treatment-naive HIV-1-infected patients. 13. On October 15, 2010, Clinical Infectious Diseases (Volume 51, Issue 8, Pages 963-972) published the 48-week results of the ASSERT study by Stellbrink HJ, Orkin C, Arribas JR, and colleagues. This study compared changes in bone density and turnover with abacavir-lamivudine versus tenofovir-emtricitabine in HIV-infected adults. 14. On July 17, 2013, AIDS (Volume 27, Issue 11, Pages 1771-1778) published the 96-week results of a randomized dose-ranging study by Stellbrink HJ, Reynes J, Lazzarin A, and others. This study evaluated dolutegravir in antiretroviral-naive adults with HIV-1. 15. In February 2012, Lancet Infectious Diseases (Volume 12, Issue 2, Pages 111-118) published the planned interim 48-week results of the SPRING-1 study by Van Lunzen J, Maggiolo F, Arribas JR, and colleagues. This dose-ranging, randomized, phase 2b trial assessed once-daily dolutegravir in combination therapy in antiretroviral-naive adults with HIV.
